SMTO-HTTP-0012 — The request went to a different website than its connection

GUID: fc22947f-fdbb-49f9-a21a-cc7b5a0ac80d
Slug: http-connection-origin-mismatch
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • Each web service connection only works with the one website address it was set up for. SMTO tried to use it for a different address, so the request was blocked and not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to set up a separate connection for the other website, then repeat that request. A connection made for one website can't be used for another, but a new connection for that site can.
  2. If the request should have gone to the connected website, compare the address with the connection's Base URL in Parameter Store. Check http versus https and any port number. Even a small difference, like a different port or https instead of http, counts as a different website.
  3. If the Base URL was wrong, correct it, select Save, then select Test connection before asking SMTO to try again. A corrected Base URL lets new connections match the address the service really uses.

What success looks like

  • The request runs and SMTO shows the service's reply instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to turn off the website-address check; it stops your sign-in details from being sent to the wrong site.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • HttpConnections.resolve blocked a request because the profile's normalized base origin or the resolved request URL differs from the origin bound to the connection recipe.

What this means

  • The normalized profile origin or resolved request URL differs from the origin bound to the connection recipe. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The normalized profile origin or resolved request URL differs from the origin bound to the connection recipe.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare scheme, host and port of the bound origin and resolved request URL, including relative-path resolution.

How to fix it

  • HttpConnections.resolve compares origin(base_url) and origin(urljoin(base_url, url)) with the recipe's bound origin. Create a separate connection (http.connect) for the intended origin, or correct the request URL or saved base_url; keep origin binding intact.
  • Create a connection for the intended origin; keep origin binding intact.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The request remains within its connection's exact bound origin.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
